title: Chapter 26: Climate Change, Global Warming and Greenhouse Effect

blocks.content: Climate change refers to long-term alterations in temperature, precipitation, wind systems, and other elements of climate over decades or centuries. While climate has naturally fluctuated throughout Earth's history, the current phase of warming is primarily driven by human activities.
1. Climate Variability vs Climate Change

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The natural greenhouse effect maintains Earth's livable temperature, but anthropogenic activities have accelerated global warming.
Major greenhouse gases include Carbon Dioxide (CO2), Methane (CH4), Nitrous Oxide (N2O), and Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs).
Global Warming Potential (GWP) measures how much energy 1 ton of a gas absorbs compared to 1 ton of CO2 over a given timeframe.
India's policy response is framed around the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) and Updated Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs).
Mitigation reduces source emissions and enhances carbon sinks, whereas Adaptation modifies systems to cope with climate impacts.

blocks.content: Climate variability refers to short-term natural fluctuations such as El Niño events, whereas climate change refers to persistent long-term shifts in global climate patterns.
2. Greenhouse Effect – Fundamental Mechanism
The greenhouse effect is the process by which certain gases in the atmosphere trap outgoing longwave radiation, keeping Earth warm enough to support life.
• Incoming solar radiation is shortwave radiation.
• Earth emits longwave terrestrial radiation.
• Greenhouse gases absorb and re-radiate this heat.
• Without greenhouse effect, Earth's average temperature would be about -18°C instead of +15°C.
Major Greenhouse Gases
3. Global Warming
Global warming refers specifically to the rise in Earth's average surface temperature due to increased greenhouse gases.
• Global average temperature has risen by about 1.1°C since pre-industrial times.
• Polar regions are warming faster (Arctic amplification).
Mitigation aims to avoid the unmanageable, while adaptation aims to manage the unavoidable.
• Glaciers and ice caps are melting.
• Sea levels are rising due to thermal expansion and ice melt.
4. Carbon Cycle and Human Disruption
The carbon cycle regulates the exchange of carbon between atmosphere, oceans, soil, and living organisms.
• Photosynthesis removes CO₂ from atmosphere.
• Respiration and decomposition release CO₂.
• Burning fossil fuels adds excess carbon.
• Oceans absorb nearly 30% of anthropogenic CO₂.

blocks.content: 5. Evidence of Climate Change
• Rising global temperatures.
• Melting glaciers and Arctic sea ice.
• Increasing frequency of extreme weather events.
• Coral bleaching.
• Ocean acidification.
6. Impacts of Climate Change

cells: Crop failure due to heat stress and irregular rainfall

Kyoto Protocol vs Paris Agreement: Kyoto established binding targets for developed nations (Annex I), while Paris relies on voluntary Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) for all nations.
India's NDC targets by 2030 include reducing emissions intensity by 45% (from 2005 levels) and achieving 50% cumulative electric power installed capacity from non-fossil sources.

List of 8 NAPCC Missions: Solar, Enhanced Energy Efficiency, Sustainable Habitat, Water, Sustaining the Himalayan Ecosystem, Green India, Sustainable Agriculture, and Strategic Knowledge for Climate Change.
